2014_068_070814mtg.paragraph: Agenda and full board packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of July 8, 2014, held at 7:00 PM in the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. Contents include a consent agenda of four sets of June 2014 minutes, teacher hires, the appointment of Remo Roncone as Principal of Troy High School effective July 9, 2014, MHSAA membership for August 1, 2014 through July 31, 2015, a cooperative girls' gymnastics agreement with Avondale School District, six technology and construction bid awards, and Superintendent Richard M. Machesky's 90-Day Entry Plan. The largest award proposed is $498,160.00 to Apple Computers for 1040 iPad Airs.

Agenda packet for the regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education on July 8, 2014, at 7:00 PM in the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, telephone 248.823.4000. The cover notes that board meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. when school is in session, and can be viewed at http://vimeo.com/troyschools. CONSENT AGENDA (Item 5). Four sets of minutes are presented: the June 3, 2014 Board of Education meeting; the June 10, 2014 Special Board of Education Meeting; the June 10, 2014 Board of Education Workshop; and the June 17, 2014 Board of Education meeting.

June 3, 2014 meeting (Athens High School). President Philippart called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. Present in addition to Ms. Philippart were Board members Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Schmidt, and Underwood; also present were Superintendent Fowler; administrators Birmingham, Brasington, Duda, Fulcher, Jolly, Keeling, Kwasny, Machesky, Rajter, and Witt; and approximately 400 members of the audience. Mike Jolly and the Board recognized All-State winter athletes including Ellen Barker, Erika Barker, Troy Chen, Zachary Chen, Brandon Goodes, Alexa Jones, Thomas Keyes, Kaylee Lee, Nicole McAllister, Julia Meng, Jeff Merola, Hye-Kyung (Matilda) Seo, Christina Shabet, Tytiana Steele, and Katherine Ward, along with a lengthy list of senior scholar athletes who maintained a 3.5 cumulative grade point average. Additional recognitions covered the Sodexo Future Chefs program, in which Wattles Elementary second grader MaryJane Ware won the national Healthy Sandwich Challenge, beating more than 2,000 elementary students from approximately 1,000 Sodexo-served schools in 30 states; the NAMM Foundation's Best Communities for Music Education designation; Wass Elementary student Norah O'Neill's Troy Community Coalition "Incredible Kid" award (nominated by teacher Nicole Schulte); perfect scores in the American Mathematics Competition by Boulan Park students Heather Gu, Shivani Konduru, James Li, Muyang Wang, and Freddie Zhao (advisor Jennifer Taylor); a first-in-nation American Scholastic Challenge sixth-grade team of Tuhin Chakraborty, Arlene Chen, Dhatri Medarametla, Pratham Soni, and Kevin Zhou (advisor Tammy Gilbert); Chemistry Olympiad results for Jonathan Li, Steven Cheng, and Stephen Li; C-SPAN StudentCam second prize for Frank Boudon (advisor Scott Gibbons); Wass fourth grader Jayanti Rakshit's national first place in the Constitution Day Poster Contest with a $50 savings bond; DECA awards at the state conference at the Amway Hotel in Grand Rapids; Destination ImagiNation global finalists; Future Problem Solvers; Troy High student Kunal Garg's first-in-state Skandaleris Business Plan win for "Your Foods," earning $1,000 plus $200 for best presentation; National German Exam gold awards for Justin O'Connell, Palkin Rampal, and Connor Welborn; HOSA national qualifiers; Michigan Japanese Quiz Bowl winners Parker Decraene, Hui Yi Liu, and Claire Nord (advisor Mina Mori); MATHCOUNTS; Lions Club Peace Poster winner Brianna Naughton; Larson Middle School's Michigan Green Schools status; Michigan Youth Arts Festival exhibitors Autumn-Joy Kendricks and Mika Obayashi (advisor Jennifer McLellan); MITES state winner Patrick Faubert (advisor Tim Heath); All-State Middle School Band participants (advisors Joe Havrilla, Scott Crecelius, Ray Torres); National Language Arts League results; National French, Japanese, and Spanish exams; perfect ACT Explore scores; Scholastic Art & Writing Awards, including Troy High's Ellen Zhang, to be honored at Carnegie Hall; the Boulan Park Advanced Orchestra's straight first division ratings at State Orchestra Festival on May 2, 2014 at Thurston High School in Redford (director Kathleen Griffith); WordMasters; Astronomy Quiz Bowl winners Steven Li and Dhruv Medarametla (advisor William Hevel); Chinese Bridge speech contest third places for Mark Elinski and Katherine Schlafhauser (advisor Sue Lin); Business Professionals of America national competitors Muhammad Qureshi, Juliana Tu, and Endri Vangjeli (advisor Elena Wollborg); Designer Genes winners Richard Mu and David Wu; Euro Challenge semi-finalists from International Academy-East; Science Olympiad Forensics winners Stephen Li and Angela Xiao; the Boulan Broncos FTC robotics team; Geologic Mapping winners Omkar Shende and Elizabeth Sun; Go Green Youth Challenge winner Ellen Zhang; Log1 and Mandelbrot math results (advisor Kevin Ortwine); National Biology Test, in which Richard Mu placed 33rd internationally among 4,161 participants and Troy High placed 5th of 298 schools (advisor Rebecca Brewer); National Brain Bee winner Chunhua Ni, 7th nationwide; National History Day state winners Frank Boudon and Jason Ji; National Math Madness; National Scholastic Press honorable mentions for Annamarie Cappetto, Megan Falk, and Courteney Roberts (advisor Jayna Salk); Neuroscience for Kids poetry winner Alex Liu; Robofest qualifiers Christian Hausner, Austin Ye, and Eric Zhong; Rocket City Math first in the nation; the Science and Engineering Fair of Metropolitan Detroit at Cobo Hall; State Fish Art winner Elizabeth Sun; the Verizon Innovative App Challenge state title for the "Optimal Forage" app; Stock Market Game; U of M Dearborn's 9th Annual Engineering and Computer Science Competition, where Frank Boudon and Aditya Das won first for Simulation (advisor Jeff Moore); USAMO national competitors Dhruv Medarametla, Lawrence Wu, and Justin Xu, with Spencer Liu and Freddie Zhao in the Junior Olympiad; the USA Biology Olympiad, taken by 7,766 students nationwide, with 12 Troy High semifinalists; Athens student Apurva Virkud's qualification for the 2014 World Youth Chess Championships in Durban, South Africa; Blackstone LaunchPad Make It Better winners (advisor Marianne Marzolla); Model UN Best Delegate Faraz Khan (advisors Sue Syme and Bill Adams); Siemens Competition recognition for ten Troy High students; the Intel International Science and Engineering Fair, where IA-East student Guangning An won a Second Award with a $1,500 cash prize and a foundation Second Award carrying a $500 savings bond (advisor David Lyons); JET Memorial Invitation Program honoree Claire Nord; and All-State High School Band winner Kyle Katynski.

June 3 actions: Resolution 14-059, moved by Mr. Schmidt and supported by Mrs. Edmunds, issued a two-year probationary contract without tenure to Ms. Melanie O'Neil as Principal, Barnard Elementary School, effective July 1, 2014 (Yes 7, No 0). Resolution 14-060, moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Mrs. Fleming, issued the same to Mrs. Sarah Glasser as Principal, Hamilton Elementary School, effective July 1, 2014 (7-0). Resolution 14-061, moved by Mr. Miletti and supported by Mrs. Edmunds, set a public hearing on the proposed budget with statutory notice at least six days in advance including the 11-point bold-faced statement that the property tax millage rate proposed to be levied to support the proposed budget will be a subject of the hearing; as printed, the resolution text specifies a hearing on June 18, 2013 at 7:00 p.m. at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois Road, Troy 48098, on the proposed 2013-2014 budget (7-0). Resolution 14-062, moved by Mrs. Fleming and supported by Ms. Underwood, awarded the parking lot/walkway lighting bid to McNulty Electric, Inc. in the amount of $342,700.00 as an expenditure of the 2014 Capital Projects Fund (7-0). Ms. Jennifer Lee addressed the board on the attendance portion of the District's Performance-Based Compensation policy and class sizes. Student representatives Michaela Smith (Athens), Needa Toofanny (International Academy-East), and Patty Durell (Troy High) reported; Naven Karoumy (Niles Community High School) was absent. Mr. Miletti announced the TFEE Golf Outing for Friday, June 20; Dr. Philippart announced a Board Workshop for Tuesday, June 10 at 6:00 p.m. The meeting adjourned at 9:12 p.m.; minutes submitted by Karl D. Schmidt, Secretary.

June 10, 2014 Special Board Meeting (Administration Building). Called to order at 5:32 p.m. by President Philippart; present were Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, and Miletti, with Schmidt and Underwood absent; administrators Fowler, Kerry Birmingham, Mark Dziatczak, Jan Keeling, Rich Machesky, Mark Rajter, and Jasen Witt attended, with approximately four members in the audience. Resolution 14-063 (Hauff/Fleming) issued a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure to Mr. Mark Dziatczak as Assistant Superintendent, Secondary Instruction, effective July 1, 2014 (Yes 5, No 0, Schmidt and Underwood absent). Resolution 14-064 (Edmunds/Miletti) approved the contract of the Superintendent of Schools, in effect from July 1, 2014 through June 30, 2017, without tenure in the administrative position (5-0). Resolution 14-065 (Fleming/Edmunds) awarded the marching band uniforms bid to Fred J. Miller, Inc. in the amount of $97,062.00 as an expenditure of the 2014-2015 General Fund (5-0). Resolution 14-066 (Miletti/Fleming) awarded playground equipment relocation to Rolar Property Services, Inc. in the amount of $129,955.00 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund (5-0). Dr. Fowler noted an upcoming discussion on extending administrative contracts to include steps frozen the prior year, informed by a salary survey of surrounding districts. Adjourned 5:54 p.m.

June 10, 2014 Board Workshop. Called to order at 6:05 p.m. with Philippart, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, and Miletti present; Schmidt and Underwood absent; administrators Fowler, Keeling, Machesky, and Rajter attending, plus five Troy High School students and approximately three audience members. Agenda: public communication; THS entrepreneurship students on the Skandalaris Business Plan Competition; 2013/2014 budget update including the final appropriation amendment and the 2014/2015 budget; discussion of Board self-evaluation recommendations; other; adjournment at 9:40 p.m.

June 17, 2014 meeting (Services Building). Vice President Miletti opened at 7:00 p.m. with the public hearing on the 2014-2015 proposed budget. Mr. Rajter presented a PowerPoint covering tax values, homestead and non-homestead forecasts, the foundation allowance, increased student enrollment, and general fund revenues and expenditures. Troy teacher Cindy Shankin asked how pupil enrollment is calculated; Rajter described a blend of low, medium and high projections and birth rate numbers and a conservative approach subject to adjustment after the official count day in September 2014. The hearing closed at 7:20 p.m. Present with Miletti were Edmunds, Fleming, and Hauff; Philippart, Schmidt, and Underwood were absent; administrators Birmingham, Dziatczak, Keeling, Machesky, Rajter, Washington, and Witt attended with approximately seven audience members. Resolution 14-067 approved consent-agenda minutes from May 5, May 6, May 15, and May 20 (4-0). Resolution 14-068 extended the contracts of Jan Keeling (Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction), Mark Rajter (Assistant Superintendent, Business Services), and Jasen Witt (Assistant Superintendent, Human Resources) through June 30, 2016 (4-0). Resolution 14-069 extended administrative contracts through June 30, 2016 for Lara Dixon, Ryan Brinks, Audra Melton, Joe Duda, Timothy Fulcher, Joyce Brasington, Janice Brzezinski, Brian Canfield, Jerry Cottone, Tammy DiPonio, Matt Jansen, Charles Lesser, Stephanie Miller, David Pass, Jeremy Whan, Melissa Curth, Robert E. Dowd, Bettie A. Goss, James Johnson, Remo Roncone, William Turner, Amy Buchanan, Jonathan Cross, Diane Kocenda, Anthony Morse, Michael Jolly, Kerry Birmingham, Kenneth Miller, Dominick Asaro, Sara Konieczka, Anne Mull, Mark Washington, Shawna Veit, and John Schiesler (4-0). Resolution 14-070 amended the 2013-14 appropriations: General Fund $136,412,506; Special Revenue Funds $8,296,343; Debt Service Funds $12,287,912; Capital Projects Maintenance Fund $100,000; Internal Service Fund $25,000. Resolution 14-071 approved the 2014-15 appropriations and millage rates: General Fund $132,525,180; Special Revenue Funds $7,840,568; Debt Service funds $16,444,718; Capital Project/Capital Projects-Maintenance Funds; Internal Service Funds $24,000; millage of 18.0000 mills non-homestead general operating, 11.2580 mills commercial personal property general, 5.2580 mills homestead general operating, and 4.7000 mills debt retirement on all properties. Resolution 14-072 awarded food services equipment and installation to Stafford-Smith, Inc. for $101,968.00 from the 2013-2014 Food Services Fund. Resolution 14-073 awarded science hardware to Sehi, Inc. for $29,550.66 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund. Resolution 14-074 awarded computers to Sehi, Inc. for $181,432.82, with $89,440.80 from the 2013-2014 TRIG grant and $91,992.02 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund. Resolution 14-075 awarded Mobile Device Management Software to CDWG for $208,921.50 from the 2014-2015 General Fund. Anita Wilson spoke on the lack of diversity among teaching staff and administration; Leonard teacher Nadeen Brown spoke on Performance-Based Compensation attendance requirements. A year-in-review slideshow was shown, and the Board thanked Dr. Fowler at her last board meeting before retirement. Adjourned 8:10 p.m.

PERSONNEL (Item 6). Probationary contracts for 2014-2015 are recommended for Kelly Pasternak, 1.0 FTE Resource Room at Wattles Elementary (B.S. Wayne State University, April 2009, Elementary Education major and Cognitive Impairment minor; M.A. Grand Valley State University, May 2012, Educational Leadership; Michigan Provisional Certificate May 2009; Dean of Support Services at Reach Academy, Roseville, July 2011-June 2013 and Resource Room teacher there July 2009-June 2011; resident of Royal Oak) and Lauren Welch, 5th Grade at Leonard Elementary (B.S. Wayne State University, December 2010, Elementary Language Arts; Michigan Provisional Certificate February 2011; long-term guest teacher in Troy School District October 2013-June 2014 and Warren Consolidated February 2013-June 2013; guest teacher with Professional Education Services Group, Caledonia, December 2010-February 2013; resident of Grosse Pointe). Item 6.B recommends Mr. Remo Roncone as Principal, Troy High School, effective July 9, 2014, on a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure; Roncone joined Troy in December 2005 as Assistant Principal at Troy High after five years as a social studies teacher in the Bloomfield Hills School District, and holds a Bachelor of Arts in History (1999), a Master of Education in K-12 Educational Administration (2005), and an Education Specialist degree in the Principalship (2012).

CURRICULUM (Item 7). The MHSAA membership resolution enrolls the six secondary schools under the Board's direction in the City of Troy, County of Oakland, as members of the Michigan High School Athletic Association, Inc. and in its approved interschool athletic activities, effective August 1, 2014 through July 31, 2015, adopting the association's Constitution, By-Laws, and HANDBOOK rules. Item 7.B renews a cooperative Girls' Gymnastics team with the Avondale School District, with Troy High School as host, for the 2014-15 and 2015-16 school years, citing declining participation.

BUSINESS (Item 8). 8.A: Chromebook hardware for a pilot at International Academy East, awarded to CDWG for $51,240.00 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund; a June 2, 2014 memo from Director of Technology Mark Washington to Superintendent Barbara Fowler describes 30 Chromebooks for teaching staff and 90 Chromebooks in three mobile carts for IA East, a net gain of 30 units, with a cart of iPads and a cart of 30 Windows laptops redeployed. Pricing under the MDE TRIG purchase plan: Lenovo Chromebook x131e, part 2214898, $334.00 each, quantity 120, $40,080; Chrome Management Console, part 2214899, $30.00, quantity 120, $3,600; Warranty 3 Yr. Depot, part 2214901, $63.00, quantity 120, $7,560; total $51,240, for 120 Lenovo Chromebooks, plus a $70/machine rebate from MDE, expensed from the 2014 Bond Fund, Phase One. 8.B: Food services equipment and installation, bid package 9790, sent to 4 potential bidders with 3 responding; reviewed by Ken Miller, Executive Director of Maintenance & Operations, Todd Hensley, Purchasing Supervisor, and Gayle Moran, Sodexo Manager; awarded to Stafford-Smith, Inc. for $77,780.00 from the 2014-2015 Food Services Fund, replacing fryers at Baker, Boulan Park, Larson and Smith Middle Schools, with the District responsible for modifications to the fire suppression system, natural gas, water, drainage, and electrical supply lines. Bid tabulation totals: Great Lakes Hotel Supply Company $77,988.00, Sam Tell and Son, Inc. $81,003.72, Stafford-Smith, Inc. $77,780.00; the Unox Model XAV 915G combi oven was quoted at $16,695.00 per unit by Great Lakes and Stafford-Smith and $17,413.20 by Sam Tell. 8.C: iPad storage cabinets awarded to CDWG for $55,775.00 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund; a June 28, 2014 memo to Superintendent Richard Machesky notes over 1200 new iPad Minis for K-2 classrooms in 10-packs and, after review of 19 cabinet models, recommends 115 Anthro iPad Cabinets (Mfg. Part# TAB16SS/PW, CDW# 2831068, NJPA contract) at $485.00 each for $55,775.00, wall-mounted, installation by Fall 2014. 8.D: Secure entrance renovation and theater upgrades at Troy High School, reviewed by Kenneth Miller and Ronald Curtis, Senior Project Manager for Barton Malow (26500 American Drive, Southfield, Michigan 48034), bid package 9788 / Series 1 Bid Package 7, proposals received June 26, 2014: General Trades to Precision Contracting Group $144,500.00; Fixed Auditorium Seating to Irwin Seating Company $130,048.00; Electrical to Metro Electric Engineering Tech. $54,800.00; total bid $329,348.00 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund. The budget for the work is $550,000, resulting in a variance of $220,662 to be applied to overages from previous bid packages, with $30,000 budgeted separately for a theater curtain not in the package. American Seating bid lower at $126,012.98, a difference of $4,035.02, but TMP Associates judged the sample chair back "overly flexible" versus the "more stable" Irwin seat, and Irwin was the basis of design for aisle lighting. Other bids: Construction Solutions $163,700.00, NACE $167,780.00, Telescopic Seating Systems $139,670.55, Shoreview Electric $87,000.00; alternates included Irwin's plastic armrests deduct $4,500.00 and demo removal deduct $9,000.00 with a clarification of $160/chair, American Seating's Core model deduct $4,957.26, and TSS deducts of $3,983.64 and $2,500.00. 8.E: Auditorium stage equipment and installation for the Athens and Troy High auditoriums, bid package 9784, reviewed by Gino Minchella, Todd Hensley, and Ken Miller, awarded to Advanced Lighting & Sound, Inc. for $425,492.38 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund, comprising communication equipment $87,221.26 and auditorium lighting $338,271.12. Competing grand totals were $527,195.00 from Great Lakes Power & Lighting, Inc. and $587,030.74 from Metro Electric Engineering, Inc.; Sound Engineering, Inc. bid $100,774.50 for communication equipment only with no bid on lighting. 8.F: iPad Airs awarded to Apple Computers of Cupertino, California, for $498,160.00 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund; a July 2, 2014 memo recommends 1040 iPad Airs at 479/each, purchased through the MDE TRIG bid tool with an additional rebate, noting iPad2 trade-in value of as much as $175/unit on as many as 750 units and a plan to sell the iPad2s originally intended for third graders. The distribution list covers iPad Air quantities of 360 for 4th grade carts, 360 for 5th grade carts, 120 for 7th grade carts, 120 for 8th grade carts, 975 for 6th grade students and 800 staff units; 1200 iPad Minis for K-2 classroom 10 packs; 120 14" testing laptops in four district sets; 2000 student iPad Air cases for grades 4-8, 850 staff cases, 1250 iPad Mini cases for K-2, and 1000 iPad2 cases for 3rd grade students, who will continue using existing iPad2s.

OTHER (Item 10). Superintendent Richard M. Machesky, Ed.D., presents his 90-Day Entry Plan, dated July 1, 2014, under the banner "One Team, One Plan, One Goal" and the district theme "All Means All!" The plan restates the district mission of ensuring learning for all members of the school community, the vision of an exemplary learning community, and goals that all students be on track to be college/career ready in literacy, mathematics, science, and social studies. Its stated purpose is a seamless transition from Assistant Superintendent to Superintendent using a "seek first to understand" practice, with immediate focus on Board relations, building on the district's "lighthouse" tradition, organizational capacity, public image, and fiscal stewardship including oversight of the 2013 Bond project. The anticipated outcome is an Executive Summary Report of findings, observations, and tentative timelines that will also direct the TSD Strategic Plan and the Superintendent's evaluation. Five goals are set out: Goal #1 Student Achievement (review achievement data and gaps, instructional improvement and intervention systems, alignment of standards, curriculum, assessment and professional development, and Central Office alignment); Goal #2 Board Governance; Goal #3 Organizational Alignment; Goal #4 Community and Public Relations; and Goal #5 Line Support Functions including Human Resources, Finance, Technology and Operations, which includes assessing readiness for collective bargaining scheduled for 2015 and reviewing long-range technology plans.
